issue.body:
Card view requests up to 14 recent runs per DAG. The first 50 cards can therefore create up to 700 independent Chakra tooltip roots and state machines, even though only one tooltip per card can be active at a time.

Reuse one multi-trigger tooltip root per DAG card. Keep every recent-run bar visible and clickable, and resolve the selected run's existing tooltip details through `Tooltip.Context` when the user focuses or hovers a trigger.

I tested it locally and it feels slightly faster. 

No visual change is expected.

issue.title: Progressively load interactive elements of Dag Card

labels.name: area:UI
labels.description: Related to UI/UX. For Frontend Developers.

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Follow-up to #69681.

The DAG Card view can render up to 50 cards with 14 recent runs per card. On cached navigation, rebuilding hundreds of run bars and repeated interactive controls can delay the page even though most cards are below the viewport.

This change renders every card shell and its static DAG information immediately, while deferring the expensive interactive content until the card approaches the viewport:

- pause, trigger, favorite, delete, and review controls
- full schedule and asset-expression UI
- recent-run bars
- run-state badges

The cards share one `IntersectionObserver` per scroll root. Hydration is one-way, so scrolling away does not unmount controls or disturb focus or open menus. The observer finds the actual scrolling ancestor and applies a 600 px `rootMargin`, avoiding a dependency on the newer `scrollMargin` option. Keyboard focus entering a deferred card hydrates its controls, and browsers without `IntersectionObserver` fall back to eager rendering.

This is intentionally not list virtualization. All card shells, DAG names, DAG identity links, sorting behavior, and browser find are available immediately. Interactive controls and recent-run links for fully offscreen cards appear when their card approaches the viewport or receives focus. All cards eventually hydrate, so the final page state is unchanged.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42ad0846-4c71-4cd2-ae8d-261690a8f4dc


Closes: #69609

### Testing

- 31 focused Vitest tests covering shared-observer behavior, scroll-root selection, one-way hydration, keyboard focus, fallback behavior, cleanup, stable geometry, and card interactions
- targeted ESLint and Prettier checks
- full UI TypeScript check with `pnpm tsc --noEmit`
- production Vite build and Airflow `prek` UI hooks
- `git diff --check`
- live Breeze sort, scroll, hover, keyboard, and exact run-link smoke tests

(72 Hours is the minimum reaction time you can expect from volunteers) - we sometimes miss notifications.

In case of an existing issue, reference it using one of the following:

* closes: #ISSUE
* related: #ISSUE
-->

closes: #66947

Each Dag card and table row on the Dags list now shows the task instance states of the Dag's recent runs as clickable badges, like the "Recent Tasks" column in Airflow 2. The counts cover all running Dag runs, or the most recent run when none is running. Clicking a badge opens the task instance list filtered to those runs and that state.

### What changed
- **New endpoint**: `GET /ui/dags/recent_task_instance_state_counts`. It takes the latest run ids the Dag list already returns (`dag_run_ids`, bounded by the API max page limit) and counts, in one statement, the task instances of each Dag's running runs, or of that latest run when none is running. Each entry returns the counted `run_ids` and the `state_counts`.
- **Card view**: he badges appear in the card's second row, under Latest Run and Next Run, next to the run state badges.
- **Table view**: a new "Recent tasks" column with an info tooltip explaining what is counted. The badges stay on one line.
- **Dynamic badges**: only the states present are shown, ordered by priority. Task instances with no state yet appear as `no_status`.
- **Links**: each badge opens Task Instances filtered by the Dag, the counted run ids and the state. These are pattern filters, so another Dag whose id starts with this one and shares a run id can also show up.
- **Setting**: "Show recent tasks" (on by default) hides the column and badges and skips the request entirely.

Unlike the run state badges from #67242, which count a Dag's runs by state, these count the task instances of its recent runs.

### Query performance
The counts come from a single statement whose size does not grow with the number of running runs. Running runs are found through the partial `idx_dag_run_running_dags` index and their task instances through `ti_dag_run`, so the cost scales with the task instances actually counted. In a local benchmark (postgres 14, Airflow's indexes, 100 Dags × 1,050 runs × 30 tasks), it was roughly 40 to 75 times faster than counting with one UNION ALL branch per run once Dags had 50 running runs each. Absolute timings depend on the machine.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3fcbe51-55d7-4d41-bde7-f15dd5481c5c
